stem: A family carries a pathogenic variant in an X-linked gene. A boy with an XY chromosome complement has manifestations, while his XX sister has the variant on one X chromosome and a normal copy on the other. Her manifestations are milder. Which of the following best accounts for this difference?

options.label: A
options.text: A second normal copy reduces expression in the brother
options.explanation: The boy's stated chromosome complement contains one X chromosome. At this X-linked locus, the additional normal X copy belongs to his sister rather than him.
options.misconception: Assigns the additional normal X-linked copy to the sibling who has only one X chromosome.

options.label: B
options.text: Two pathogenic copies are required in the brother
options.explanation: A boy with one X chromosome can express an X-linked pathogenic allele without a second X-linked copy. Requiring two copies misapplies a recessive autosomal model.
options.misconception: Applies a two-copy autosomal requirement to a boy with one copy of the X-linked locus.

options.label: C
options.text: The variant lies on a nonsex chromosome in the sister
options.explanation: The gene is explicitly X-linked in both siblings. Moving it to an autosome in one sibling does not follow from their different levels of expression.
options.misconception: Treats different phenotype severity as evidence that the gene changes chromosome location.

options.label: D
options.text: The sister lacks the variant found in her brother
options.explanation: The sister's variant is established in the stem. Her milder expression must therefore be interpreted despite carriage, not explained by assuming she lacks the allele.
options.misconception: Equates milder expression with absence of a variant that testing has already established.

options.label: E
options.text: A second normal copy reduces expression in the sister
options.explanation: The sister has a nonmutated copy at the X-linked locus, whereas the brother has one X chromosome. This can reduce expression without guaranteeing an absent phenotype.
options.misconception: No misconception: The sister has an additional normal copy that can lessen expression of the variant.

context: Learning objective: use gene-copy context when interpreting X-linked disease expression. The sister has a second nonmutated copy, while the brother has one X-linked copy; the difference does not establish a universal rule for females.
